decisions.question: Where does the manifest live?

options.label: Postgres
options.why: parts_done flips in the same transaction as the part write; one more table to migrate

options.label: S3 object
options.why: all upload state in one system; every part becomes an ETag-conditional write with retries, about a day more in step 2

decisions.why: parts_done flips in the same transaction as the part write; one more table to migrate

decisions.question: Who owns the idempotency key?

options.label: Server id
options.why: the manifest id is the key; no SDK change beyond step 6; a client that loses it starts over and pays once per completed file

options.label: Client key
options.why: survives a client that retries POST /uploads itself; costs a (customer, key) unique index, a 409 path, and SDK changes in every language

decisions.why: the manifest id is the key; no SDK change beyond step 6; a client that loses it starts over and pays once per completed file

decisions.question: How long before an upload is abandoned?

options.label: 24 hours
options.why: bounds blob storage at one day of interrupted uploads; mobile clients on flaky networks almost always retry within hours

options.label: 7 days
options.why: safer for very large uploads over bad links; up to a week of orphaned parts per abandoned upload and a sweeper scan that grows with it

decisions.why: bounds blob storage at one day of interrupted uploads; mobile clients on flaky networks almost always retry within hours
